name: Trajectory Transformer
summary: Offline RL as one big sequence-modeling problem: every state dimension, action dimension, the reward and the reward-to-go are discretized into 100 bins and become separate tokens of a small GPT. There is no learned encoder and no policy network; acting is beam search over the model's own trajectory predictions, extended one token at a time. Latency scales with state dimensionality, and the authors note it can take seconds per action, which rules out real-time control.

name: TransDreamer
summary: The first transformer world model in the Dreamer setting. The Transformer State-Space Model (TSSM) replaces the RSSM's GRU: the deterministic state h_t is a causal transformer over the past stochastic latents and actions, one token per step, and the posterior drops h_t so every step trains in parallel. Everything else is DreamerV2: CNN encoder and decoder, discrete latents, reward and discount heads, actor-critic in imagination. The transformer is tiny (2 layers), so imagination is latency-bound per step and attention over the growing imagined history is the only cost that scales.

name: IRIS

name: SlotFormer
summary: The reference object-centric dynamics model. A frozen SAVi (or STEVE) encoder turns each frame into a handful of object slots, and a small transformer encoder over the slots of the last T frames predicts all of the next frame's slots in one pass, then rolls out autoregressively. There are no actions; rollouts feed video prediction, VQA and PHYRE planning. The transformer sees only tens of tokens per step, so the encoder and the per-slot spatial-broadcast decoder carry most of the compute.

name: TWM
summary: A Dreamer-style agent whose dynamics model is a causal Transformer-XL instead of a GRU. A CNN VAE turns each 64x64 observation into 32x32 categorical latents; latent, action and reward enter as three separate tokens per step, and the hidden state read from the action token drives MLP heads for the next latent, reward and discount. name: RAP (Reasoning via Planning)
summary: The template for using an off-the-shelf LLM as a world model. A frozen LLaMA-33B is prompted three ways: as the policy that proposes actions, as the world model that writes the next state in natural language, and as the reward model. Monte Carlo tree search runs 10-20 iterations over these text states before one answer is committed. Every tree expansion is a full LLM generation, so inference is serial 33B decoding inside a search loop, with no training at all.

name: REM
summary: An IRIS-style token world model whose transformer is replaced by a Retentive Network and whose per-token decode loop is removed. Retention keeps a fixed-size recurrent state instead of a KV cache, and Parallel Observation Prediction (POP) feeds 64 learned prediction tokens from that state to sample all 64 next-frame codes in one call. Imagination becomes 2 calls per frame instead of 64, which the authors measure as 15.4× faster than prior token-based world models.

name: Cosmos Policy
summary: Cosmos-Predict2-2B Video2World, a latent video diffusion transformer over Wan2.1 VAE latents, fully fine-tuned into a robot policy with no architectural change. Proprioception, the action chunk and the value are injected as extra latent frames: blank images are VAE-encoded and their latents overwritten with tiled copies of the vectors, so the denoising process that predicts future images also predicts actions. As a direct policy it denoises everything in parallel in 5 steps (0.61 s per chunk on one H100) and discards the future state and value; planning mode decodes them autoregressively for best-of-N search.

name: LingBot-VA
summary: A causal world-action model that interleaves video latents and actions in one autoregressive sequence with a KV cache. Two parallel transformer streams of the same depth, a 5B video stream initialised from Wan2.2-5B (d 3072) and a 0.35B action stream (d 768), are joined by shared attention. Each step denoises the next chunk of 4 latent frames with 3 Euler steps only to s = 0.6 (partial denoising, enabled by noisy-history augmentation), then decodes the 16 actions as inverse dynamics in 10 steps; real observations re-enter the cache in closed loop.

name: DreamZero
summary: A 14B world-action model: the Wan2.1-I2V-14B image-to-video DiT is fully fine-tuned into a chunk-wise autoregressive flow-matching model that denoises the next 2 latent frames of video and the matching 1.6 s action chunk together, with one shared timestep and separate output decoders. Clean context sits in a KV cache of at most 8 latent frames, and after each chunk executes the predicted frames are replaced by encoded real observations. Naive inference costs 5.7 s per chunk; CFG on 2 GPUs, velocity caching (16 → 4 steps), compilation, NVFP4 and the 1-step DreamZero-Flash schedule bring it to 150 ms on 2 GB200.

name: comma.ai world model (openpilot 0.11)
summary: The learned driving simulator behind openpilot 0.11, the first shipped driving policy trained entirely inside a world model. A ViT compressor turns the two camera views into a 32x16x32 latent, and a 2B block-causal diffusion transformer predicts the next frame latent from 2 s of context, 6-DoF relative-pose actions and 1 s of future frames (so it is also an inverse dynamics model). Sampling is frame by frame with 15 Euler steps and CFG 2.0; with KV caching comma reports 12.2 frames/s per GPU, a batched training-throughput number rather than an interactive latency.

2B diffusion transformer: 48 layers, d 1600, 25 heads (n_layer=48, n_head=25, n_embd=1600), 'adapted to 3 dimensional data'

summary: Skywork's 720p successor to Matrix-Game 2.0, built on Wan2.2-TI2V-5B. name: SANA-WM
summary: A minute-scale camera-controlled world model whose DiT replaces most softmax attention with frame-wise Gated DeltaNet: 15 of 20 blocks keep a D×D recurrent state per head, updated once per latent frame, and only 5 blocks use softmax attention, run at deployment with an attention sink plus a local window. The LTX2 VAE packs 8 raw frames into one 128-channel latent frame, so 60 s of 720p fits one GPU. Self Forcing distillation gives a 4-step chunk-causal generator; with NVFP4 on one RTX 5090 it denoises 60 s of 720p in 34 s (authors).

name: Matrix-Game 3.5
summary: Matrix-Game 3.5 returns to a fully causal generator and moves memory out of the KV cache into geometry: historical VAE-latent patches are lifted to 3D with metric depth, re-projected into the target view and inserted as tokens, so each 3-latent-frame chunk attends to a bounded pose-aware sequence of noisy targets, one clean anchor, a few context frames, patch-memory tokens and a reference prefix. Camera pose enters through tiled PRoPE with no new parameters. A 3-step causal student reaches 20 fps at 1280x704 on one H100 with INT8, GPU retrieval and a 75%-pruned decoder (company claim).

Block-causal chunks of 3 latent frames over one pose-aware sequence: noisy targets + clean anchor + context frames (1 per chunk in causal training, up to 5 in base training) + patch-memory tokens (≤1 per target cell) + a reference prefix of ≈1 frame; ≤≈7,900 tokens per chunk [D], bounded by ≈2.3x the target track; training window 1 anchor + 7 chunks = 22 latent positions

Camera pose via tiled PRoPE in every block: after RoPE, queries × Pᵀ, keys and values × P⁻¹, outputs × P, tiled over all head channels, no new parameters; translations recentred on the first target frame and log-compressed

Perceptual flow matching causal adaptation (10k steps), then curriculum self-rollout DMD (1,000 outer steps, 5:1 update ratio) → 3-step causal generator; prefix and chunk-local context held at the next noise level each substep (HiAR), anchor clean
MG-LightVAE, 75%-pruned Wan2.2 decoder → 12 frames per chunk at 1280x704; 'VAE decoding becomes the primary latency bottleneck' once the DiT is accelerated

Patch memory (MosaicMem-style): patches lifted to 3D with metric depth and poses, frustum-queried, z-buffered and scattered into a target-aligned memory frame; retrieval and dynamic-object filtering run once per segment, off the per-frame loop; the sequence does not grow with rollout length

Up to 20 output frames/s at 1280x704, batch 1, one H100, including the INT8 3-step DiT, online retrieval and MG-LightVAE decode (company claim; the VLM prompt rewriter runs asynchronously); 10.9 one-minute videos/hour at 77.0 GB peak on one H100 in the SANA-WM benchmark, undistilled model (authors' Table 1)

Memory is geometry, not cache: the per-chunk sequence is capped at ≈2.3x the target track, so DiT cost is constant in rollout length and the depth, lift and projection work sits off the per-frame critical path
